items.title: Being a quasi-compact immersion is fpqc local on the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is a quasi-compact immersion' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 6262-6266). The proof fixes an fpqc covering, writes the base changes f_i, and assumes each is a quasi-compact immersion; these are separated, so descent of quasi-compactness and separatedness makes f quasi-compact and separated; the scheme-theoretic image factorization X -> Z -> Y is then formed, the closed subscheme Z being cut out by Ker(O_Y -> f_* O_X) because f is quasi-compact; flat base change (using separatedness of f) identifies f_{i,*} O_{X_i} with the pullback of f_* O_X, so Y_i x_Y Z is cut out by the pullback of the ideal, whence each X_i -> Y_i x_Y Z is an open immersion by the characterisation of quasi-compact immersions; descent of open immersions then makes X -> Z an open immersion, so f is an immersion, quasi-compactness having already been established (proof lines 6268-6300). The level is H3: the ideal-theoretic description of the scheme-theoretic image and its base change is the load-bearing computation, and it is carried out explicitly.
